speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; to understand the pattern of your right knee pain and swelling, along with your episodes of urinary pain and previous left ankle episode, can you tell me if the current knee pain occurs at night or wakes you up?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive arthritis (Reiter's syndrome) secondary to untreated urethritis. The combination of asymmetric oligoarthritis affecting the lower limbs (left ankle history, current right knee), dysuria, young age, sexual activity with multiple partners, and inconsistent condom use strongly supports this diagnosis. I will now request a Urinalysis and request images of the affected joints.
